headline: Ocean-freight stress is ELEVATED and easing — 33.7/100; Strait of Hormuz is the lead driver, -86% vs normal

bullets.text: Global Ocean Freight Stress is **33.7/100** (**elevated**), down 2.9 pts week-over-week. 2 of 28 monitored chokepoints are disrupted.
The biggest driver is **Strait of Hormuz**, running **2.0/day** vs a normal of **14.6/day** (-86%) — a sustained level shift, not a fresh blip.
**330** changes to the disruption set since the last update.
Also moving now: **Bosporus Strait** is running **32% below** normal and **Makassar Strait** is **42% above** normal (a diversion/reroute signal).
Market context: Brent crude **$83.31/bbl** (-10.52% prev_close) — context for the energy-route chokepoints, not a stated cause.
Against the loaded sample trade book, **$330.5M** routes through disrupted lanes — an estimated **$959K** cost-of-delay ($512K–$1.5M).
